answer: Stake bonding is the concrete anti-Sybil mechanism: every agent identity must lock capital proportional to the weight it claims, and the protocol slashes that bond when duplicate farming or collusion is proven. A farm of puppet accounts therefore needs fresh capital behind each one, and attack cost rises linearly with the number of sybils instead of staying flat. Honest agents keep their bond working like orchard rows, compounding yield over time, while an attacker holds a velvet bond it cannot withdraw, and the visible horizon of profit drops below the capital at risk.
